items.title: Mozambique’s 2027 budget framework sees narrower deficit, modest growth
items.summary: The budget framework, which now goes to parliament, projects a 2027 deficit of 4.6% of gross domestic product (GDP), down from a forecast of 7.0% of GDP in the 2026 budget Economic growth in 2027 is seen at 1.6% The 2026 budget predicted growth of 2.8%, but recent projections from international institutions are less optimistic The International Monetary Fund estimates 1.0% growth this year for the resource-rich southern African nation, versus 0.5% predicted by the African Development Bank A heavy debt burden is one of Mozambique’s most pressing economic challenges Problems date from a 2016 hidden-debt scandal that wrecked investor confidence and curbed access to funding Matters have been worsened by delays to major natural gas projects that had been expected to boost exports, revenue and government finances

items.title: Netflix to shed 1,000 jobs in steepest cuts since 2022
items.summary: Netflix has said it will cut 1,000 jobs globally as the streaming giant faces competition from rivals The cuts - the steepest since 2022 - will mainly affect its human resources, legal, product and technology teams and equates to around 6% of its total workforce Last month, Netflix 's co-chief executive, Ted Sarandos, told the Bloomberg Screentime summit that the company was "not growing as fast as I want us to" The streaming industry is going through a period of consolidation following Paramount's $110bn (£83.6bn) merger with Warner Bros, the owner of HBO, while free platforms such as YouTube and TikTok continue to attract viewers In an email to staff, Sarandos and co-chief executive Greg Peters said Netflix would "continue to invest aggressively in high-impact areas to improve our service and further drive growth and innovation" Netflix had come close to its own deal with Warner Bros but was outbid in the end by Paramount Commenting on the "organisational changes", Sarandos and Peters said: "Our mission - to entertain the world - is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to…

items.title: Mozambique: INAM warns of intense heat in Maputo, Gaza and Inhambane until Sunday
items.summary: According to a weather warning issued on Wednesday, 14 October, the conditions are due to the continued influx of hot, humid air masses, which are expected to affect several districts and cities across the three provinces In Maputo province, the phenomenon is expected to affect mainly Boane, Namaacha, Moamba, Magude, Manhiça, Marracuene and Matutuíne, as well as the cities of Maputo and Matola In Gaza province, the areas at risk include the districts of Chibuto, Guijá, Mapai, Chicualacuala, Mandlakazi, Chókwè, Massingir, Mabalane, Massangena and Limpopo, as well as the city of Xai-Xai In Inhambane province, intense heat is expected to affect mainly Zavala, Mabote, Funhalouro, Panda and Inharrime INAM also noted that high temperatures would continue to affect the central region of the country, particularly districts along the Zambezi Valley In view of the forecast, the institute recommends taking precautionary and safety measures to reduce the risks associated with intense heat The next INAM weather bulletin is scheduled for Thursday, 15 October, at 10:00 a.m

items.title: Nord Stream trial opens in Germany, defense seeks dismissal
items.summary: Serhii Kuznietsov is accused of attacking civilian infrastructure in the 2022 sabotage of the Russian gas pipeline to Germany. His lawyers called Nord Stream a military target, and said their client is sworn to secrecy The trial of a former Ukrainian special forces officer, Serhii Kuznietsov, opened in the northern German city of Hamburg on Wednesday amid considerable public and press interest Kuznietsov is accused of leading the September 2022 sabotage operation that put the undersea Nord Stream 1 and 2 gas pipelines linking Russian to Germany out of action .

items.title: Climate change and drone attacks exacerbate the humanitarian crisis in war-torn Sudan
items.summary: Aid groups warn of an imminent collapse of the health system as fighting continues to displace civilians amid the planting season. The UN has extended an arms embargo, but only for Darfur In Sudan , clashes between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) have intensified in North Kordofan and parts of Blue Nile state. The fighting has forced thousands of civilians to flee amid the planting season Since war broke out between the two factions and their allied militias in April 2023, both sides have fought for power . However, neither has managed to establish control over the entire country The SAF, the nation's official army, is in control of Sudan's north and center, including the capital, Khartoum, while the RSF maintains its presence in the western Darfur region and parts of the south The brutal war has plunged Sudan into one of the world's worst humanitarian and displacement crises, according to the United Nations and international aid organizations.

items.title: Zimbabwean author denies using AI to write award-winning story
items.summary: Simbarashe Kundizeza says he was inspired by a poem about fish tanks to write a story about his family struggles in Zimbabwe Zimbabwean writer Simbarashe Kundizeza has denied using artificial intelligence (AI) to write his short story, which won this year's Caine Prize for African Writing His statement comes a week after he scooped the £10,000 ($13,000) award and a recent article in The Atlantic said AI-detection software Pangram had shown his work about a boy whose family falls on hard times was entirely AI generated "For the avoidance of doubt, I wrote The Blue Fighter," he posted on X , external The accusation has caused an uproar on social media and Caine Prize chair Ellah Wakatama told the BBC she was shocked that the US magazine had not waited for a full investigation before publishing "I do wish The Atlantic had spent more time investigating this so that alongside Pangram, they did have evidence of real human investigation of it before tainting the prize and tainting this winner," Wakatama told the BBC's Front Row programme The chair of the Caine Prize's board of trustees…

items.summary: Turkish authorities have raided the Istanbul offices of Halk TV, halting broadcasts, appointing a trustee and opening an investigation.
